data.title: ONE Championship: Chatri defends Haggerty over Akimoto knee – ‘There was no foul’
data.description: ONE Championship boss Chatri Sityodtong has defended Jonathan Haggerty’s disputed knee against Hiroki Akimoto, citing slow-motion footage to reject claims of an illegal strike.

data.title: Suvarnabhumi runway subsidence probed after plane gets stuck
data.description: The Ministry of Transport is investigating runway subsidence at Thailand’s biggest airport, Suvarnabhumi, after the landing gear of a China Airlines plane got stuck in the runway surface.

data.title: Bangkok Post secures website following brief disruption
data.description: The Bangkok Post website experienced a brief technical disruption on Thursday morning after unauthorised content appeared on its homepage and other pages.

data.title: ‘Sin tax’ revenue shake-up draws fire
data.description: Four proposed legal amendments could put about 14 billion baht a year in funding for health promotion, public broadcasting, elderly welfare and sports development at the government's discretion, prompting public opposition to plans to end their automatic share of alcohol and tobacco tax revenue.

data.title: Mbappe and Real face long road to redemption in China
data.description: HONG KONG - Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won’t be easily or quickly repaired, experts say.

data.title: ONE Championship: Chatri confirms Di Bella title defence for ONE 174 in December
data.description: Jonathan Di Bella will defend his ONE Championship strawweight kickboxing title at ONE 174 in December, as the promotion revives its numbered series even sooner than March’s planned return to Qatar.

data.title: PM denies solar project favours big firms
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Wednesday criticised media reports linking major corporations, including Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc, to the government's household solar rooftop scheme, rejecting claims that the project was designed to favour large businesses.

data.title: Myanmar workers wanted for employer’s killing surrender
data.description: Two married couples from Myanmar, wanted in connection with the killing of their Chinese employer in Bangkok, have surrendered to police after hiding in sugarcane fields in Phanat Nikhom district of Chon Buri.

data.title: Nurses oppose community volunteer plan
data.description: The Nurses Association of Thailand has opposed the government's Community Nursing Volunteer initiative, urging authorities to review the policy and promote oversight to protect patient safety and healthcare standards.

data.title: Antonelli ready to rewrite F1 record books in Mexico
data.description: MEXICO CITY - Kimi Antonelli will take his place in Formula One’s record books as the youngest champion and Italy’s first since 1953, barring a wild swing of unexpected misfortunes amid a fiesta atmosphere at this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix.

data.title: No need for stockpiling, Ministry of Defence clarifies
data.description: Thailand’s Ministry of Defence issued a statement on Thursday clarifying that the public does not need to stockpile food, water or medical supplies in response to escalating tensions in the Middle East.

data.title: Pinehurst Golf Club & Hotel : A Championship 27-Hole Golf and Lifestyle Destination Near Bangkok
data.description: Combining championship golf, a two-level driving range, four-star accommodation and comprehensive lifestyle facilities, Pinehurst Golf Club & Hotel offers Thai and international golfers a convenient destination for sport, relaxation and quality time—all in one place.

data.title: Get your pasta passport  for 'The Taste of Italy'
data.description: The Embassy of Italy in Bangkok, Thailand, invites lovers of Italian cuisine to enjoy their favourite dishes and earn prizes during "Taste of Italy Passport: Discover. Taste. Collect. Unlock", which will take place throughout November.

data.title: Hello Kitty firm apologises, scraps TV tie-up after China anger
data.description: BEIJING - Sanrio, the Japanese company that owns the popular Hello Kitty character, apologised on Thursday over its tie-up with a TV spy drama criticised as anti-China, cancelling a merchandise collaboration with the show.

data.title: Falklands War munitions fashioned into ‘Chalice of Peace’ for the pope
data.description: BUENOS AIRES - Combining the remnants of shell casings and other items from the Falklands War, Argentine silversmith Juan Carlos Pallarols is crafting a "Chalice of Peace" to give to Pope Leo XIV when he visits Argentina next month.

data.title: ‘My blood was spilled here’: Tanzania election violence not forgotten
data.description: DAR ES SALAAM - A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.

data.title: EU and Canada to open ‘new chapter’ at Montreal summit
data.description: MONTREAL, Quebec - Canada and the European Union will craft “a new chapter” in their alliance at a summit that opens on Thursday, the EU chief said, as they navigate uncertain relations with the United States.

data.title: Indonesia in  focus during 'Sudo Rungu'
data.description: Indonesian contemporary artist Roby Dwi Antono is now showcasing his first solo exhibition in Thailand titled "Sudo Rungu: Echoes Of Fire", which draws on memories from his father who worked as a blacksmith, at Moca Museum of Contemporary Art from now until Jan 3.

data.title: Thai property groups seek mortgage tax relief and property tax changes
data.description: Three associations seek to double the mortgage interest deduction cap and revise land and building tax categories as buyers face limited purchasing power and tight credit.

data.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles into East Sea
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea fired short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul’s defence ministry said, less than a week after South Korea proposed talks over a growing border row.
